evidence: Falsification run against the installed Claude Code 2.1.261 with a temporary plugin whose root carries only .claude-plugin/plugin.json ({"skills":"./skills/"}), one skill, and a conventional hooks/hooks.json registering SessionStart and Stop command hooks that create marker files: `claude -p --safe-mode --tools '' --strict-mcp-config --mcp-config '{"mcpServers":{}}' --setting-sources '' --plugin-dir <plugin> --output-format stream-json --verbose --no-session-persistence` exited 0, init listed the plugin, and neither marker was created. The identical invocation without --safe-mode created both markers, so the probe can detect hook execution and the negative result is attributable to safe mode.

claude_review.sh refuses with capability_missing when the CLI lacks --safe-mode and always passes the flag (the probe suite pins both: a CLI without --safe-mode is refused, and the recorded argv of every owner-aware run carries --safe-mode), so the loaded plugin's conventional hook surface is disabled on every path that reaches --plugin-dir; the CLI's own --safe-mode help text names hooks among the customizations it disables.

Residual, recorded rather than closed: the containment rests on the CLI's safe-mode contract, which the wrapper checks by flag presence only; a future CLI that ran an explicitly loaded plugin's hooks under safe mode would re-open this path, and the manifest-key check would not catch a conventional hooks/ directory. The installed ccl-skills plugin does ship hooks/hooks.json without a manifest hooks key, which is why the probe used the same layout.
